questions.text: "The new compound is ___ more effective than the existing treatment." (considerably — strong difference)
"The ___ stringent the peer review process, the ___ reliable the published findings." (proportional)
questions.hint: "The more X, the more Y" = proportional structure

questions.text: "The open data approach was ___ effective as the closed data approach." (equal or near-equal)
questions.hint: "Not quite as + adjective + as" = slightly below equal

questions.text: "The data ___ a link between sleep deprivation and cognitive performance." (medium hedging verb)
"___ 80% of participants responded positively in the first trial." (surprisingly high maximum)
questions.hint: "As many as + number" = surprising maximum figure

questions.text: "It remains ___ whether the intervention works equally well across all age groups."
questions.hint: "It remains unclear whether + clause" = impersonal hedge

questions.text: "The treatment ___ reduce symptoms in the majority of patients." (theoretical possibility)
"Open data practices ___ to be associated with significantly higher replication rates." (cautious verb)
questions.hint: "Appear to be" = hedging phrase — cautious assertion

questions.text: "___ 200 participants were enrolled in the study." (standard approximator)
"Of the two methodologies, the second is ___ rigorous." (comparing exactly two)
What is the "replication crisis"?
opts: Scientists duplicating each other's work unnecessarily
The failure to replicate many widely-cited scientific findings
A shortage of research funding for replication studies
The difficulty of repeating experiments with limited resources
questions.correct: The failure to replicate many widely-cited scientific findings

questions.text: "There is ___ evidence that exercise reduces the symptoms of depression in adults." (some but not definitive)
questions.hint: "There is some evidence that" = cautious positive claim

questions.text: "___ the data we collect, ___ our understanding of the phenomenon becomes."
questions.hint: "The more X, the richer Y" = proportional structure

questions.text: "The results were more better than expected" is grammatically correct.
What is the "winner's curse" in science?
opts: A prize given to the first person to publish a finding
The tendency for early, small studies to overestimate effect sizes
The competitive pressure on scientists to make breakthrough discoveries
The reward for challenging an established paradigm
questions.correct: The tendency for early, small studies to overestimate effect sizes

questions.text: "It is ___ that the sample size will need to be increased for the effect to reach significance."
questions.hint: "It is likely that + clause" = formal impersonal hedging

questions.text: "Pre-registration is becoming ___ and ___ common in clinical research." (progressive increase)
"___ 50 replications have been attempted — the minimum for a robust estimate." (confirmed minimum)
According to Reading 2, what is "publication bias"?
opts: A preference for studies from prestigious universities
The tendency to publish positive findings while ignoring null results
Bias in the choice of journal topics
The influence of corporate sponsors on research outcomes
questions.correct: The tendency to publish positive findings while ignoring null results

questions.text: "The new drug performed ___ as expected based on the Phase 1 trials." (slightly below equal)
questions.hint: "Not quite as + adverb + as" = slightly below equal

questions.text: "The new analysis was ___ more thorough than the original one." (far — strong difference)
A fortuitous discovery made by chance during unrelated investigation is called ___.
Which sentence uses hedging correctly for scientific writing?
opts: "This study proves that mindfulness reduces anxiety."
"This study may possibly perhaps suggest that mindfulness might help."
"These findings suggest that mindfulness may reduce anxiety in some populations."
"Everyone knows that mindfulness definitely reduces anxiety."
questions.correct: "These findings suggest that mindfulness may reduce anxiety in some populations."

questions.text: "As many as 80% responded positively" implies a surprisingly high maximum figure.
questions.hint: "As many as + number" = used for surprisingly high maximum

questions.text: What is "pre-registration" in research?
opts: Signing up early for a research conference
Registering a hypothesis and methodology before collecting data
Submitting a paper before peer review is complete
Applying for a research grant before the study begins
questions.correct: Registering a hypothesis and methodology before collecting data
